claim: zero of the 20 contain an executable step list; the brief greps 3 keys
correction: the brief's 3 keys miss a FOURTH executable form the tree ships and tests: [[composite.stage]] (F289 D2, v0.7.0rc6, tests/test_byo_cascade_toml.py). It is 0 here too, so the CONCLUSION stands — but the MECHANISM for an executable cascade-catalog descriptor already exists and is not the ADR-0008 one.

claim: the engine has never been used to generate an op; Phase 2 never happened
correction: Phase 2 PARTLY happened. The engine ships, has a C run loop (srmech_chain_run, rc173/rc174), and executes 7 chains across 3 attested catalogs — including a real 9-step composition (friedmann_dark_fraction) that threads @row and @step[N] refs. What is true is NARROWER and sharper: every one of the 15 shipped steps is class N. The engine has never composed ACROSS classes.

claim: (not in the brief) why every shipped chain step is class N
correction: ADR-0008 §3.1 hard-binds `class` to a fixed letter->module map. 19 of the 20 cascade-catalog ops are not exposed by ANY mapped module — the atoms live in srmech.cascade.atoms / .composites / .hypercomplex_dft, which no letter points at. Class N is the only letter whose module (srmech.math.rational) happens to hold callable ops. The single-class shipped corpus is a CONSEQUENCE of §3.1, not a preference.

claim: the engine has no DAG / branching / chain-level iteration, all explicitly Phase-2 scope
correction: True of srmech.cascade.compose. NOT true of the tree: srmech.dsl's [[stage]] schema already ships loop_n / sub_chain / fold_init / fold_op / reduce_op / parallel_body — the chain-level iteration ADR-0008 §11 defers. The tree has THREE declarative composition surfaces, not one, and the RICHEST control flow is not in the ADR-0008 one. A Phase 2 spec written against compose.py alone would re-invent shipped machinery.

claim: the chain value contract admits only None / int64 / float / str / list / tuple — no carrier, no dict, no bignum
correction: That contract is the NATIVE run-loop marshal (compose.py:_reconstruct_value), not the engine's. The pure path threads all 18 carriers tested — Mat, Vec, HV, Q, Qi, CDRegister, SedenionRegister, dict, bignum, complex — with object IDENTITY preserved across the step boundary. The C loop returns _NATIVE_MISS rather than mis-marshalling, so the narrow contract costs SPEED, never correctness. Rung 2's premise is therefore false as stated, which is why rung 2 passes.

claim: (found on the way) CHANGELOG.md:251 explains why best_rational_signed fails the `composes` AST clause
correction: The explanation is a MISDIAGNOSIS. No interpreter runs this op — the pure path calls all three by hand at composites.py:205 / :212 / :214. Two of the three ARE AST-reachable from the parent body; `best_rational` is invisible to a NAME scan solely because it is imported under the private alias `_best_rational`. The gate was loosened for a reason that does not hold, so it is now weaker than the evidence warranted. Also note the body calls builtin `round()` and `int()` — the two operations this spike had to supply as an unregistered Class-N op.
